name: OnKey
works_with: Mac with Apple Silicon. Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube in a browser
short: A free Mac singing trainer that listens to the song you're playing and shows where your pitch is off.
what: OnKey is a singing trainer for the Mac. You play a song in Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube and sing along. The first time you get the lyrics, and OnKey learns the singer's melody when the song ends. After that the notes scroll towards you, your pitch is drawn over them, and you get a score with a report on every line.
who: Anyone who sings at home and wants to know when they're off key. You need an Apple Silicon Mac. It isn't meant for bars or events, where the README points you to a licensed karaoke service.
needs: A Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later)
Music you're entitled to play, in Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube in a browser

steps.title: Download and install
steps.text: Download `OnKey.dmg` from the latest GitHub release, open it and drag OnKey to Applications.

steps.title: Grant permissions
steps.text: Setup asks for the microphone, to hear you, and for system audio recording, to hear the music app. When it asks whether it may follow Spotify and Apple Music, you can choose Listen only and it follows songs by their sound alone.

steps.title: Sing a song twice
steps.text: Play a song and sing along. The first play gives you lyrics and teaches OnKey the melody. On later plays you get the scrolling notes and a score.

steps.title: Or build it yourself
steps.text: You need the Xcode command line tools, Rust, Node and Python 3. A self-built copy can't ask Shazam to name new songs.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/dsmurrell/onkey && cd onkey
npm install && npm --prefix ui install
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r scripts/requirements-models.txt
PYTHON=.venv/bin/python scripts/fetch-models.sh   # downloads the models and checks them by SHA-256
npx tauri build

try.label: From the README
try.text: Play a song you like in Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube, sing along, then play it again to see your pitch against the notes.

watch: It needs microphone and system audio recording access.
It never saves the music, and your recordings stay on your Mac. A take sung over speakers can contain some of the music.

Some requests go out: a short sound signature to Shazam to name songs, the song details to LRCLIB for lyrics, iTunes lookups for covers, and a daily update check to GitHub. Settings has switches for Shazam, lyrics and the update check.
The README asks you not to share the melody transcriptions it makes, and not to post screen recordings with the music playing.
